s1.syndrome_frame: Acute unilateral vision loss with eye pain and signs of intraocular inflammation
salient_findings: Blurry vision and pain in one eye
Whitish focal granuloma at the pupillary margin
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Symptoms started 4 days prior to presentation
Recent routine dental cleaning 1 week prior
No history of gingival disease or cavities
Visual acuity was 20/25 OD and 20/50 OS initially
Intraocular pressures were 15 mm Hg OD and 11 mm Hg OS
Left eye examination showed conjunctival hyperemia and keratic precipitates
3+ cells with fibrin in the anterior chamber
Mild nuclear sclerosis
Whitish focal granuloma at the 4-o'clock position at the pupillary margin
Posterior segment was unremarkable
Gram stain revealed gram-positive cocci in chains and gram-positive rods in a branching pattern
Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute unilateral vision loss with eye pain and signs of intraocular inflammation
salient_findings: Blurry vision and pain in one eye
Whitish focal granuloma at the pupillary margin
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Symptoms started 4 days prior to presentation
Recent routine dental cleaning 1 week prior
No history of gingival disease or cavities
Visual acuity was 20/25 OD and 20/50 OS initially
Intraocular pressures were 15 mm Hg OD and 11 mm Hg OS
Left eye examination showed conjunctival hyperemia and keratic precipitates
3+ cells with fibrin in the anterior chamber
Mild nuclear sclerosis
Whitish focal granuloma at the 4-o'clock position at the pupillary margin
Posterior segment was unremarkable
Gram stain revealed gram-positive cocci in chains and gram-positive rods in a branching pattern
Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius

differentials: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
per_call: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy

shortlist.label: Endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of intraocular inflammation, hypopyon, and positive culture results

shortlist.label: Bacterial endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain and culture results indicating bacterial infection

shortlist.label: Streptococcal endophthalmitis
shortlist.why_kept: Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius, a specific type of bacterial infection

shortlist.label: Uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Intraocular inflammation and presence of keratic precipitates

shortlist.label: Iridocyclitis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammation of the iris and ciliary body, consistent with clinical findings

raw.rationale: The presence of gram-positive cocci in chains and the aerobic culture revealing Streptococcus intermedius, along with the clinical presentation of decreased visual acuity, conjunctival hyperemia, and a whitish focal granuloma, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Endophthalmitis
rejected.why: Too broad, as the specific causative organism is identified as Streptococcus intermedius

rejected.label: Bacterial endophthalmitis
rejected.why: Also too broad, as it does not specify the type of bacteria, which in this case is Streptococcus

rejected.label: Uveitis
rejected.why: Uveitis is inflammation of the uvea, but the specific findings and culture results point more specifically to an infectious cause, namely Streptococcal endophthalmitis

rejected.label: Iridocyclitis
rejected.why: Iridocyclitis refers to inflammation of the iris and ciliary body, but the presence of a granuloma and positive culture for Streptococcus intermedius indicate a more severe, infectious process like endophthalmitis
